title: Redwood data retention demo - Cascade Payments
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Cascade Payments through the Console and API controls for data handling: request storage toggles, field redaction, PII detection, and retention policies. Customer wants SOC2 artifacts, confirmation of API header to disable storage, and a pilot to validate redaction on real transaction samples.
next_steps: Send security whitepaper, SOC 2 report, and encryption whitepaper
Share short recording of the retention toggle demo and Console walkthrough
Provision test tenant for Cascade and enable pilot with sample dataset
Schedule a technical benchmark for request throughput with storage toggles off
action_items: Maya Chen: Send security whitepaper + SOC2 report (due: 2026-03-15)
Devon Patel: Share retention toggle demo recording and step-by-step config notes (due: 2026-03-13)
Alex Rivera: Provide sample PII patterns and expected retention policy for pilot (due: 2026-03-18)
Samir Khan: Confirm KMS vendor and compliance contact info (due: 2026-03-16)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros?
[00:08] Alex (Cascade): Alex here, CTO. Samir and Priya from engineering and security also on.
[00:12] Maya: Great, I'll hand over to Devon — he'll walk through the Console and the API toggles for request storage and redaction, and then we'll answer questions.
[00:20] Devon (Redwood SE): Hi all, yeah thanks. I'll share my screen — let me know if the deck or Console looks off.
[00:28] Samir: We're mostly interested in how we can avoid storing transaction payloads, how PII is redacted, and what audit trails we keep for compliance.
[00:36] Devon: Totally — our goal today is to show two paths: Console toggles and API-level headers. Console first: under Settings > Data Handling you can toggle "Store requests" per-tenant or per-route.
[00:48] Devon: If you flip it off, by default the platform will not persist request or response text to long-term storage; ephemeral caches for in-flight inference still operate but we don't write to logs. Note: we keep minimal audit metadata for billing and SLOs unless you request complete opt-out.
[01:05] Priya: When you say "ephemeral caches" do you mean KV cache? Is anything persisted locally on the GPU host?
[01:11] Devon: Good question. The KV cache is in-memory and is not written to disk under our standard hosted model. For Dedicated or Private on-prem, admins can enable disk-backed caches — but that is configurable and we can advise how to mount ephemeral volumes.
[01:24] Maya: Also worth flagging that our Private deployment supports full air-gapped setups and you can use your own KMS/HSM for keying.
[01:30] Alex: Show us the exact Console flow — we want to screenshot and show our security team.
[01:34] Devon: Sure — switching to Console: here is the tenant page; under Data Controls -> Request Storage we have three options: Store All / Store Redacted / Do Not Store.
[01:45] Devon: "Store Redacted" runs our PII detection pipeline and redacts by pattern and ML detection (card numbers, SSN-like patterns, emails, phone numbers). We also allow custom redaction rules you can upload as regexes.
[01:59] Jordan (Customer Dev): Regexes — can we upload a list of tokens to always mask?
[02:03] Devon: Yep, you can upload a policy file or add route-level overrides. The Console also surfaces a Preview that shows how example input would be redacted.
[02:12] Priya: Is that preview deterministic? If we send the same request twice will it redact the same way?
[02:17] Devon: For pattern-based redaction yes; for ML-based contextual redaction we aim for consistency but there can be slight differences. We log redaction events to the audit trail with hashes so you can verify a redaction occurred without storing the raw content.
[02:31] Samir: About audit trails — what exact metadata do you keep when Store = Do Not Store?
[02:36] Devon: Minimum metadata: timestamp, route id, model variant, token count, latency, and a hashed request id. We do not retain request or response text. Billing-related aggregates are kept per-account.
[02:45] Priya: For SOC 2 we need proof that PII is not retained. Can you provide artifact?
[02:50] Maya: Yes, we'll share SOC2 and our security whitepaper after the call.
[02:54] Alex: You mentioned API header — what's that?
[02:56] Devon: There's an API header that overrides per-tenant defaults: x-redwood-store-requests: false (or true). You can also use x-redwood-redaction: strict|lenient to pick a redaction mode.
[03:07] Alex: So we could set that header conditionally from our gateway?
[03:09] Devon: Exactly. Many customers use a middleware to strip request bodies or set the header based on route.
[03:14] Maya: Quick demo: we'll send a sample payment payload and show both behaviors. Devon, can you queue up the sample?
[03:19] Devon: Yep, sending a sample now.
[03:22] [03:22] Devon (screen): Here is a payload with card number 4242 4242 4242 4242 and an email alex@example.com. First with Store All on — you can see the raw text recorded in the live logs (blurred for demo).
[03:37] [03:37] Devon: Now flip Store to Do Not Store and re-run — the live logs show "redacted" or empty and the audit hash appears instead of raw content.
[03:44] Priya: Does redaction happen pre-flight (before any external logging) or post-flight? We need to ensure no intermediate logs capture sensitive fields.
[03:50] Devon: Redaction occurs upstream in our ingestion layer before any persistent logging. Inter-process traces might carry masked tokens only. We can walk you through the ingestion diagram in the security doc.
[04:02] Samir: For throughput, does turning off storage change latency? There's concern about increased CPU for redaction or pattern checks.
[04:09] Devon: Great point — toggling storage off slightly reduces I/O because we skip writes; redaction, if enabled, adds a small CPU cost (~5-10% on typical request mix) but we have an opt-in fast-path that uses lightweight regex first. We can run a benchmark on your workload.
[04:23] Alex: For Dedicated, do you still offer the same storage toggles?
[04:26] Devon: Yes, Dedicated supports the same control plane semantics. For on-prem/private, toggles are enforced by your admin — by default the control plane will push the policy but the customer-managed runtime ultimately owns storage.
[04:37] Priya: KMS — can we use our AWS KMS keys?
[04:40] Devon: Yes, we support KMS integrations. You can bring your own key, including customer-managed CMKs in AWS, GCP Cloud KMS, or Azure Key Vault. For Private deployments we also support HSM integrations.
[04:50] Maya: I'll drop the KMS integration guide in the follow-up.
[04:54] Jordan: What about logs in the console? Even if requests are not stored, is there an admin view that could show snippets?
[05:00] Devon: Admins can see redaction summaries and counts but not raw contents when Do Not Store is enabled. The Console has RBAC so you can limit who sees what.
[05:07] Priya: How does Redwood Optimize tie in — are there caching/quantization changes that affect data handling?
[05:12] Devon: Redwood Optimize is our recommendation engine — it can suggest quantization and batching profiles. It doesn't change storage semantics, but some optimize recommendations (e.g., more aggressive caching) might imply keeping prefixes in memory. Those are still ephemeral by default.
[05:28] Alex: We're interested in the API contract — can you show a curl example?
[05:31] Devon: Sure. curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXX' -H 'x-redwood-store-requests: false' -d '{"input": "..." }' . That header will instruct the platform to avoid persisting the payload.
[05:46] Samir: What happens if we set store=false but later need to debug an incident and want to rehydrate raw logs? Is there a rehydrate option?
[05:52] Devon: No — if you explicitly disable storage for those requests we can't restore raw content. We recommend sending a policy to only disable for production traffic and keep a debug route where storage is enabled or send hashed pointers to a separate secure store you control.
[06:06] Priya: Any SLA implications if we disable storage?
[06:09] Devon: None on availability; pricing/billing uses aggregated metrics. For Dedicated customers wanting forensic logs we can provide an opt-in capture for a limited window under stricter access controls.
[06:20] Maya: We also offer automatic PII detection for tokens — you can configure redaction to replace PII with deterministic placeholders so you can still correlate across requests without seeing raw values.
[06:33] Alex: Deterministic placeholders mean same value maps to same placeholder?
[06:36] Devon: Yes — we hash the PII with a salt and show placeholder like <mask:hash123>. That lets you link requests while keeping raw values hidden. The salt can be customer-managed with BYOK.
[06:48] Jordan: Any false positives on hashing? If a legitimate account number looks like a card number will it get masked?
[06:53] Devon: There is always tradeoff; we let you tune the detection and add allowlists. We can run your sample payloads to tune.
[07:03] Priya: For compliance, do you retain redaction logs with the original pattern?
[07:07] Devon: We keep event logs saying "redaction applied: pattern=email" and timestamp, plus the hash, but not the original text.
[07:16] Alex: Ok, let's talk pilot — we want to run a week of shadow traffic with redaction enabled and storage off for 10% of production. What's the onboarding look like?
[07:25] Maya: Typical pilot: 1) provision test tenant; 2) exchange KMS and network details for Private or Dedicated; 3) load sample payloads; 4) run a benchmark; 5) evaluate redaction results and metrics. We aim for 2-3 weeks to iterate.
[07:38] Samir: Any paperwork? NDA already done, do we need a DPA?
[07:41] Lena (CSM): We'll attach the DPA and data handling annex to the quote; Maya will include it with the security packet.
[07:49] Priya: One more question: is there a programmatic API to manage retention windows (e.g., set route X to 7 days)?
[07:55] Devon: Yes — there's a REST endpoint: PATCH /v1/tenants/{id}/data-controls with retention_days and store_mode. We'll include the API spec in the follow-up.
[08:04] Alex: Performance question — can we schedule a throughput test where store=false vs store=true to measure token/sec delta?
[08:10] Devon: Absolutely — we'll run a side-by-side benchmark on a representative workload.
[08:15] Maya: Wrapping up: will send artifacts and propose pilot timeline. Any last items?
[08:21] Priya: Please include the ingestion diagram and proof points for redaction happening before any logging.
[08:26] Samir: For benchmarks include p95 latency and cost delta per 1M tokens.
[08:31] Alex: We'll also share a sample of anonymized transactions for tuning rules.
[08:36] Maya: Great, we'll follow up. Thanks everyone.
[08:40] [End of recording — total 46 minutes]
